Message From The Top Management Dear Stakeholders, The global pharmaceutical industry continues to navigate a period of profound transformation. Geopolitical developments, evolving trade policies, regulatory expectations and macroeconomic uncertainties are reshaping the way healthcare businesses operate across the world. While these factors present near-term challenges, they also reinforce the importance of resilient organisations that can adapt with agility, innovate with purpose and consistently uphold the highest standards of ANNUAL REPORT 2025-2026 | 2 quality. India remains one of the most promising pharmaceutical markets globally, driven by scientific capability, manufacturing excellence and an expanding healthcare ecosystem. Yet, as the industry evolves, sustained success will increasingly depend on innovation, operational excellence and the ability to respond to changing market dynamics with speed and discipline. At Indoco, these principles have guided us for decades. As we complete another year of our journey, we are proud of how our teams have translated challenges into opportunities while remaining steadfast in our commitment to patients, healthcare professionals, customers and shareholders. Our performance during FY 2025-26 reflects the strength of this foundation. Across our businesses, we continued to build momentum through focused execution, disciplined investments and a clear strategic direction. Our Domestic Formulations business expanded its portfolio with the launch of several new products, including the introduction of Cyclopam AC, Iceraft Tablets, Triz LM, Sensodent DSP and Sensodent DCP toothpastes in the OTC segment. We also continued our strategic shift towards mass specialities, enabling a more diversified and future-ready portfolio. The growing confidence of the medical fraternity in our brands is reflected in our prescription performance. th During the year, Indoco advanced to the 20 position in the IPM, recording 10.94 crore prescriptions and moving ahead of several established industry players. Our Institution division achieved its business targets for the fifth consecutive year, while Rexidin M Forte Gel emerged as the No. 1 dentist-prescribed oral care brand. These

Suresh G Kare | Chairman Sundeep V Bambolkar | Jt. Managing Director Aditi Panandikar | Managing Director ANNUAL REPORT 2025-2026 | 3 milestones reaffirm the trust that healthcare professionals continue to place in us. Quality has always been at the helm of what we do. The successful completion of the USFDA inspection at our Patalganga API facility with zero observations, along with the successful EU GMP (European Union Good Manufacturing Practice) inspection of our Goa & Baddi formulation plants by the Malta Medicines Authority, Germany - LAGeSo authority, further demonstrates the maturity of our quality systems and our steadfast commitment to regulatory compliance. These are the result of a deeply embedded culture of excellence across the organisation. Our commitment to operational excellence also gathered further momentum. The implementation of our Master Manufacturing Plan across all the units has begun delivering measurable improvements in productivity and manufacturing efficiencies. Recognition of our Baddi manufacturing facility with the Silver Award at the National Awards for Manufacturing Competitiveness is a validation of our continuous improvement journey and our pursuit of world-class manufacturing standards. Our international business and research capabilities continued to gather momentum. During the year, we strengthened our international product portfolio with multiple USFDA final approvals. We also expanded our consumer healthcare footprint with the launch of toothpaste in South Africa. These achievements reflect our growing capability to deliver differentiated products across global markets while strengthening our international presence. Sustainability continues to be an integral part of our long- term growth strategy, guiding the way we create value for our stakeholders while fulfilling our responsibility towards society and the environment. Across our operations, we are advancing initiatives that improve resource efficiency, reduce environmental impact and strengthen operational resilience. The increasing adoption of renewable energy through our open-access solar power projects at our Patalganga and Rabale locations, coupled with focused efforts in energy optimisation, reflects our commitment to lowering our carbon footprint. The EcoVadis Bronze Medal awarded to our Patalganga API facility is an encouraging recognition of these efforts and motivates us to further elevate our sustainability journey. The awards and recognitions we received during the year, including the Champion of Quality Award from the U.S. Pharmacopeia and the Most Preferred Workplace 2025-26 Award are a tribute to the passion, integrity and dedication of every member of the Indoco family. Their commitment continues to be our greatest strength. We will continue to invest in science, innovation and differentiated products, strengthen our manufacturing capabilities, accelerate digital transformation, expand our global footprint and deepen our commitment to quality, sustainability and governance. Most importantly, we will continue to build an organisation that is agile, resilient and prepared for the opportunities of tomorrow. For almost eight decades, Indoco has evolved with changing times while remaining true to its core values. Every milestone in our journey has been built on trust earned from patients, and healthcare professionals, regulators, partners, employees and shareholders. That trust remains our greatest responsibility and our strongest motivation. We extend our heartfelt appreciation to all Indocoites for their unwavering dedication, our healthcare professionals and customers for their continued confidence, our business partners for their collaboration, and our shareholders for their enduring trust and support. Together, we will continue to advance healthcare, create sustainable value and build a healthier future.

Committed To Quality, Driven By Precision Manufacturing Excellence At Indoco, manufacturing excellence is the foundation of our commitment to delivering safe, effective, and high-quality healthcare solutions to patients worldwide. Our manufacturing capabilities are designed to meet the most rigorous standards of quality, efficiency, and regulatory compliance, ensuring that consumers worldwide receive safe and effective healthcare, consistently and reliably. Transforming Operations, Enhancing Efficiency The implementation of the Master Manufacturing Plan (MMP) across our formulation sites has delivered measurable benefits across Indoco's manufacturing network. There is a definitive direction in achieving economies of scale by adhering to larger batch sizes, automation and quality, thereby rationalizing the cost of production. This strategic initiative provides a clear roadmap for sustainable growth and operational excellence across all manufacturing sites. Quality And Compliance Focused Indoco's state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities are approved by some of the most respected regulatory agencies in the world, including the USFDA, UKMHRA, EDQM, TGA - Australia, WHO GMP, SAHPRA - South Africa, etc. ANNUAL REPORT 2025-2026 | 6

SOCIAL Empowering People. Enriching Communities. At Indoco our people are our strength and the catalysts of transformation. Their commitment, passion and expertise enable us to deliver quality and innovative healthcare while advancing our sustainability goals. We nurture a culture of respect, inclusion, well-being and continuous growth, empowering every employee to contribute meaningfully to our purpose Employee Engagement of improving lives and creating a lasting positive impact. Throughout the year, we launched a series of holistic employee engagement initiatives tailored to support the professional, physical, and emotional well-being of our teams. Comprehensive onboarding was prioritized from day one to ensure that all new team members felt welcomed and supported. Throughout the year, we championed proactive health and wellness by hosting expert-led workshops on nutrition, specialized healthcare and physical mindfulness to help employees manage stress and maintain long-term vitality. In addition to personal wellness, we reinforced organizational safety by equipping our entire workforce with vital emergency response and ﬁrst aid skills. Key cultural milestones were leveraged to bring our teams together, celebrating shared heritage and fostering a uniﬁed vision for a collaborative, progressive future. Together, these initiatives have strengthened our workplace culture, reﬂecting our deep commitment to nurturing a healthy, safe, and highly motivated workforce. ANNUAL REPORT 2025-2026 | 12

Building Skills And Driving Excellence SOCIAL Our learning and development initiatives this year focused on equipping our workforce with essential tools and skills needed to thrive in a dynamic business environment. We enhanced operational eﬃciency by introducing the LIIO (Lean Integrated Indoco Operations) framework and launched a centralized Learning Management System (LMS) to streamline digital training. To align our teams with corporate objectives, we rolled out the Indoco Goal Setting Program (IGSP) across functions and facilitated a strategic workshop on 'Thinking Organization - Co-creating the Future'. Additionally, a specialized QUEST learning series was introduced for the HR, Learning & Organizational Development and Medical Services teams, supporting the development of critical functional and leadership competencies. Indocoites enhanced their professional eﬀectiveness through focused programmes on Advanced Excel and Business Communication, critical training on Foreign Trade, Customs Regulations and FEMA compliance. Our commitment to a culture of safety, integrity and accountability remained unwavering, supported by mandatory learning initiatives on GMP, Workplace Safety, POSH, Behavioural Standards and Labour Laws. Through these initiatives, we continue to build a skilled, agile and future- ready workforce capable of driving sustainable growth. ANNUAL REPORT 2025-2026 | 13

liable to all consequences under the IT Act 2025 and tax shall be deducted at the higher rates as provided in Section 397 of the IT Act 2025, i.e., 20% of tax deduction at source. However, no tax shall be deducted on the dividend payable to resident individual shareholders if the total dividend to be received by them during tax year 2026-2027 does not exceed ` 10,000 and also in cases where members provide Form 121, subject to conditions specified in the IT Act 2025. Resident shareholders may also submit any other document as prescribed under the IT Act 2025 to claim a lower / nil withholding of tax. PAN is mandatory for members providing Form 121 or any other document as mentioned above. For non-resident shareholders, taxes are required to be withheld in accordance with the provisions of Section 393 and other applicable sections of the IT Act 2025, at the rates in force. The withholding tax shall be at the rate of 20% (plus applicable surcharge and cess) or as notified by the GOI on the amount of dividend payable. However, as per Section 159 of the IT Act 2025, non-resident shareholders have the option to be governed by the provisions of the Double Tax Avoidance Agreement (“tax treaty” or “DTAA”), read with Multilateral Instrument (MLI), if any, between India and the country of tax residence of the shareholders, if they are more beneficial to them. For this purpose, i.e. to avail the benefits under the DTAA read with MLI, non-resident shareholders will have to provide the following: • Copy of the PAN card allotted by the Indian Income Tax authorities duly attested by the shareholders/ authorized signatory. In case of non-availability of PAN, information under sub- rule 2 of rule 217 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026. • Copy of the Tax Residency Certificate for the tax year 2026-2027 obtained from the revenue or tax authorities of the country of tax residence, duly attested by shareholders / authorized signatory. • Form 41 (for claiming tax treaty benefit), which can be obtained electronically through the e-filing portal of the income tax website at https://www.incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal. • Self-declaration by the shareholders of having no permanent establishment in India in accordance with the applicable tax treaty and IT Act 2025. • Self-declaration of beneficial ownership of equity shares by the non-resident shareholder. • Self-declaration of fulfilling all conditions of applicable tax treaty for being eligible to claim benefit of the tax treaty read with MLI. • Any other documents as prescribed under the IT Act 2025, if applicable, or certificate for lower withholding of taxes, duly attested by the shareholders. In case of Foreign Institutional Investors (FII) / Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPI), tax will be deducted under Section 393 of the IT Act 2025 at the rate of 20% (plus applicable surcharge and cess) or the rate provided in relevant DTAA, read with MLI, whichever is more beneficial, subject to the submission of the above documents, if applicable. The aforementioned documents are required to be submitted by members only through email to

EXPLANATORY STATEMENT As required by Section 102 of the Companies Act, 2013, the following Explanatory Statement sets out all material facts relating to the special business mentioned under Item No. 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 of the accompanying Notice dated July 28, 2026: Item No. 5 Pursuant to Section 148 of the Companies Act, 2013 (“Act”) read with the Companies (Cost Records and Audit) Rules, 2014, as amended from time to time, the Company is required to have the audit of its cost records conducted by a cost accountant in practice. On the recommendation of the Audit Committee of Directors, the Board of Directors approved the re-appointment of M/s. Joshi Apte and Associates (Firm Registration No. 00240) as the Cost Auditors of the Company to conduct audit of cost records of the Company for the financial year ending March 31, 2027 at a remuneration of ` 1,80,000/- (Rupees One Lakh and Eighty Thousand Only) per annum plus applicable taxes and actual out of pocket expenses. In making the decision on the appointment and remuneration of the Cost Auditors, the Audit Committee of Directors considered the Cost Auditors’ performance during the previous year(s) in examining and verifying the accuracy of the cost accounting records maintained by the Company. M/s. Joshi Apte and Associates have furnished a certificate regarding their eligibility for appointment as Cost Auditors of the Company. They have vast experience in the field of cost audit and have conducted the audit of the cost records of the Company for previous years under the provisions of the Act. In accordance with the provisions of Section 148 of the Act read with the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014, the remuneration payable to the Cost Auditors has to be ratified by the members of the Company. Accordingly, consent of the members is being sought for the passing of an Ordinary Resolution as set out at Item No. 5 of the notice for ratification of the remuneration payable to the Cost Auditors for the financial year ending March 31, 2027. None of the Directors or Key Managerial Personnel of the Company or their respective relatives are, in any way, concerned or interested, financially or otherwise, in the resolution except to the extent of their shareholding, if any, in the Company. The Board, based on the recommendation of the Audit Committee, recommends the Ordinary Resolution as set out in Item No. 5 of this Notice for approval by the members of the Company. Item No. 6 Ms. Aditi Panandikar (DIN: 00179113) was appointed as the Managing Director of the Company for a term of five (5) years commencing from February 15, 2022 till February 14, 2027. Accordingly, her term as Managing Director of the Company will expire on February 14, 2027. As per the proviso to Section 196(2) of the Companies Act, 2013 (“Act”), no re-appointment of the Managing Director can be made earlier than one year before the expiry of the term. III. Other information 1. Reasons of loss or inadequate profits The Company has continued to make strategic investments to strengthen its long-term business resilience, manufacturing capabilities, quality systems and market presence. The key factors contributing to the loss or inadequate profits during the year include: • Investments undertaken for strategic positioning and capability development in the OTC/ OTX segment, with the objective of establishing a sustainable platform for future growth. • Continued investments under the Master Manufacturing Plan (MMP) across manufacturing sites to improve productivity, enhance process efficiencies, strengthen quality standards, increase automation and optimise resource utilisation. These initiatives involve an investment phase, with benefits expected to accrue progressively over the medium to long term. • The Company’s Formulation Business in regulated markets witnessed a decline, primarily due to planned upgradation and improvement activities at its sterile manufacturing facilities. The Company is also undertaking remediation measures in accordance with the requirements of the US regulatory authority. These initiatives are focused on strengthening compliance, quality systems and manufacturing capabilities, with regulatory clearance awaited for recommencement of supplies to the US market. 2. Steps taken or proposed to be taken for improvement The Company has undertaken the following measures to improve operational efficiency, strengthen responsible manufacturing practices and support sustainable business performance: • The Company’s investment phase in the OTC/OTX segment has substantially progressed. The Company expects these investments to progressively contribute to revenue growth and operating efficiencies over the coming quarters. • The OTC/OTX business has demonstrated a positive year-on-year revenue trajectory, indicating increasing utilisation of the capabilities and infrastructure established through the investments made in this segment. • Initiatives under the Master Manufacturing Plan (MMP) have started yielding measurable operational benefits, including increased batch sizes, improved manufacturing processes, enhanced productivity and strengthened quality systems. • The Company continues to focus on automation, process optimisation, capacity utilisation and resource efficiency across its manufacturing operations, with the objective of improving productivity while maintaining stringent quality standards. • The Company is strengthening its supply chain capabilities with a focus on OTIF (On Time In Full) performance, thereby improving reliability of supplies, customer service levels and efficiency in export operations. • The Company continues to focus on remediation and quality improvement measures at its regulated-market manufacturing facilities, with the objective of ensuring sustainable compliance and strengthening its ability to serve regulated markets. 55

DIVIDEND Based on the Company’s performance, the Board of Directors recommended a dividend of ` 0.20 per equity share of ` 2/- each (10%) for the financial year 2025-2026. The dividend on equity shares is subject to the approval of the members at the Seventy-Ninth Annual General Meeting (“AGM”) scheduled to be held on Thursday, September 17, 2026. Dividend for the financial year 2024-2025 was ` 0.20 per equity share (10%). The Register of Members and Share Transfer Books of the Company will remain closed from Friday, September 11, 2026 to Thursday, September 17, 2026 (both days inclusive) for the purpose of payment of the dividend for the financial year ended March 31, 2026. According to Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations, the top 1,000 listed entities based on market capitalization, calculated as on March 31 of every financial year are required to formulate a Dividend Distribution Policy which shall be disclosed on the website of the listed entity and a web link shall also be provided in their Annual Reports. Accordingly, the Dividend Distribution Policy of the Company which is based on the need to balance the twin objectives of appropriately rewarding its shareholders with dividend and of conserving resources to meet its future needs, can be accessed using the following link: https://www.indoco.com/policies/IRL_dividend_distribution_policy.pdf.

Evaluation of Performance of the Board, its Committees and Individual Directors During the year, the evaluation of the annual performance of individual Directors including the Chairman of the Company and Independent Directors, Board and Committees of the Board was carried out under the provisions of the Act, relevant rules, and the Corporate Governance requirements as prescribed under Regulation 17 of SEBI Listing Regulations and based on the SEBI Master Circular No. HO/49/14/14(7)2025- CFD-POD2/I/3762/2026 dated January 30, 2026, with respect to Guidance Note on Board Evaluation. The Nomination and Remuneration Committee had approved the criteria for the performance evaluation of the Board, its Committees and individual Directors as per the SEBI Guidance Note on Board Evaluation. The Chairman of the Company interacted with each Director individually, for evaluation of performance of the individual Directors. The evaluation for the performance of the Board as a whole and of the Committees were conducted by way of questionnaires. In a separate meeting of Independent Directors, performance of Non Independent Directors and performance of the Board as a whole was evaluated. Further, they also evaluated the performance of the Chairman of the Company, taking into account the views of the Executive Directors and Non-Executive Directors. The Board of Directors reviewed the performance of the individual Directors on the basis of the criteria such as qualification, experience, knowledge and competency, fulfilment of functions, availability and attendance, initiative, integrity, contribution and commitment. The Independent Directors were additionally evaluated on the basis of independence, independent views, judgement etc. Further the evaluation of Chairman of the Board, in addition to the above criteria for individual Directors, also included evaluation based on effectiveness of leadership and ability to steer the meetings, impartiality, etc. 61

The Board also assessed the fulfilment of the independence criteria as specified in the Act and SEBI Listing Regulations, by the Independent Directors of the Company and their independence from the management. REMUNERATION POLICY FOR DIRECTORS, KEY MANAGERIAL PERSONNEL AND OTHER EMPLOYEES AND CRITERIA FOR APPOINTMENT OF DIRECTORS The Nomination and Remuneration Policy is intended to achieve the following objectives: 1. To formulate the criteria for determining qualifications, competencies, positive attributes and independence for appointment of a director (executive/non-executive/independent) of the Company; 2. The level and composition of remuneration is reasonable and sufficient to attract, retain and motivate directors of the quality required to run the Company successfully; 3. Relationship of remuneration to performance is clear and meets appropriate performance benchmarks; and 4. Remuneration to directors, key managerial personnel and senior management involves a balance between fixed and incentive pay reflecting short and long-term performance objectives appropriate to the working of the Company and its goals. EMPLOYEE STOCK OPTIONS / RESTRICTED STOCK UNITS The Company has adopted and implemented the Indoco Remedies Limited Employee Stock Option Plan - 2022 (“Plan”) pursuant to the approval of its shareholders at the 75th Annual General Meeting held on September 22, 2022, with an objective of enabling the Company to attract and retain talented employees by offering them the opportunity to acquire a continuing equity interest in the Company, which will reflect in their efforts in building the growth and the profitability of the Company. The Plan is implemented through the Indoco Employees Welfare Trust which will acquire the shares of the Company by way of fresh allotment from the Company and will transfer the shares to the eligible employees upon exercise by them of vested Options/RSUs within the exercise period and subject to payment of exercise price and satisfaction of tax obligation, if any, arising thereon. The Plan is administered by the Nomination and Remuneration Committee of the Company which is designated as Compensation Committee in pursuance of Securities and Exchange Board of India (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021, for the purpose of administration and implementation of the Plan.

WHISTLE BLOWER POLICY / VIGIL MECHANISM To create enduring value for all stakeholders and ensure the highest level of honesty, integrity and ethical behaviour in all its operations, the Company has a Whistle Blower & Vigil Mechanism Policy. Further details on vigil mechanism of the Company are provided in the Corporate Governance Report, forming part of this Report. INTERNAL FINANCIAL CONTROLS The Company has an Internal Control System, commensurate with the size of its operations. The Internal Audit department monitors and evaluates the efficacy and adequacy of internal control system in the Company, its compliance with operating systems, accounting procedures and policies at all locations of the Company. Based on the report, significant audit observations and corrective actions thereon are presented to the Audit Committee of the Board. The Company’s Internal Auditor also monitors and evaluates the internal control system and submits Quarterly Reports which are placed before the Audit Committee of the Board. RISK MANAGEMENT The Board of Directors has constituted a Risk Management Committee which reviews key risk elements of the Company’s business, finance, operations and compliance. The Risk Management Committee also assesses the adequacy of mitigation plans to address such risks. The Corporate Governance Report, which forms part of this report, contains the details of Risk Management Committee of the Company. Risk Management Committee has formulated and implemented Risk Management Policy in compliance with the provisions of the Act and SEBI Listing Regulations. The policy helps to identify the various elements of risks faced by the Company, which in the opinion of the Board threatens the existence of the Company. The Risk Management Policy can be accessed on the Company’s website at https://www.indoco.com/ policies/Risk_Management_Policy.pdf. Annexure-C to the Directors’ Report Annual Report on Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Activities 1. A brief outline on CSR Policy of the Company: It is the Company’s intent to make a positive difference to the underprivileged members of the society. Corporate Social Responsibility is the responsibility of the corporate entity towards the society in consideration of the support given and sacrifices made by the society, by sharing part of the Company’s profits. Indoco Remedies Limited, strongly believes that reaching out to the underserved communities is part of Indoco’s commitment to the society. The Company believes in transcending business interests and grappling with the “quality of life” challenges that the underserved communities face and are working towards making a meaningful difference to them. The Company’s mission is to improve the quality of human life by enabling people to do more, feel better and live longer. The Company intends to provide resources in terms of financial aid, medicines, time and equipment to non-profit organizations to focus on programs that are “innovative, sustainable and bring real benefits to those most in need”. The Company’s philosophy is to target support to selected programs that are innovative, sustainable and that produce tangible results. The Company intends to lend a helping hand to the underprivileged in the society through the support of women, children and the aged in the areas of health, education, public sanitation etc. Implementing this philosophy in spirit, the Company shall make a positive contribution to the communities in which it operates, and invest in health and education programs and partnerships that aim to bring sustainable improvements to these people. 2. Annexure-F to the Directors’ Report Conservation of Energy, Technology Absorption and Foreign Exchange Earnings and Outgo (Particulars pursuant to Rule 8(3) of the Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014) A. Conservation of Energy a. Steps taken or impact on conservation of energy during the financial year 2025-2026: i. Brine Chiller Optimization at Patalganga Plant: Modification carried out at Patalganga Plant resulted in single compressor working instead of two compressor working. Further the second compressor has been utilized as a Standby Compressor for reliable operation. This has resulted in energy savings of approximately 5,15,520 kWh Units amounting to ` 54.12 Lakhs. ii. The HVAC system operation has been optimized through continuous monitoring and demand-based operation at Patalganga Plant which has resulted in energy savings of approximately 1,67,904 kWh Units amounting to ` 17.63 Lakhs. iii. Boiler operating hours has been reduced due to improved efficiency at Patalganga Plant which has resulted in energy savings of approximately 1,30,904 kWh Units amounting to ` 13.74 Lakhs. iv. The HVAC system operation has been optimized through continuous monitoring and demand-based operation at Rabale Plant which has resulted in energy savings of approximately 1,35,619 kWh Units amounting to ` 14.24 Lakhs. v. Modification in Main PCC panel at Goa Plant-I has resulted in energy savings of approximately 1,29,600 kWh Units amounting to ` 9.72 Lakhs. vi. The HVAC system operation has been optimized for 12 AHUs at Goa Plant-I which has resulted in energy savings of approximately 1,10,964 kWh Units amounting to ` 8.32 Lakhs b. Steps taken by the Company for utilizing alternate sources of energy: i. At Rabale R&D Centre total solar power units generated is 25,51,712 kWh which has resulted in energy savings of 9,56,937 kWh per annum amounting to annual savings of ` 89.49 Lakhs. ii. At Patalganga Plant total solar power units generated is 34,48,518 kWh which has resulted in energy savings of 14,11,483 kWh per annum amounting to annual savings of ` 1.84 Crores. c. The capital investment on energy conservation equipment: Approximately ` 3.17 Crores B. Technology Absorption a. Efforts made towards Technology Absorption: i. Introduction of the “Defect Library” concept for Ophthalmic Container Closure System at Goa Plant II: The Defect Library is a standardized quality control tool used in pharmaceuticals that catalogs common defects, their descriptions, visuals, severity levels, and acceptance criteria to enable consistent visual inspection and prevention or arresting defects at early 87 stage of incoming inspection of packaging system.

Page 89Open in PDF ↗

c0

A Defect Library typically classifies defects by severity (critical, major, minor), provides detailed descriptions (e.g. crack length > 1mm), includes high-resolution images or illustrations, and defines AQL sampling plans for inspection. Defect Library is essential to component manufacturer as well, often drawn from real production failures or simulated examples, to train operators or inspectors, to segregate the component defects while production of components and ensures the defect free supplies of packaging systems. ii. Introduction of “TAAPI Size Estimation Chart” to measure the defect size during visual inspection at Goa Plant II: The TAPPI Size Estimation Chart (often abbreviated as TAAPI chart) is a standardized transparent tool for visually estimating defect sizes during inspections. It aligns perfectly with pharmaceutical packaging quality control needs, like spotting inclusions or flaws in films, foils, or molded components. This flexible, flat transparency (about 9x14 cm) features printed black dots and rectangles representing known areas from 0.02 to 5.00 mm2. Inspectors overlay it directly on defects - such as spots, specks, or imperfections - for quick, direct visual comparison. It’s governed by TAPPI Test Method T 564, ensuring consistent, reproducible results across operators. iii. Simplification homogenization process in Oral suspension formulations: The Oral suspension formulations are having criticality to achieve required particle size within minimum cycles of homogenization by IKA homogenizer at manufacturing plant scale. Mebeverine oral suspension and Perampanel oral suspension, both suspensions dosage form was executed at plant scale with required particle size by IKA homogenizer. iv. Scalability beyond 10 X batch size: In pharmaceutical manufacturing, scaling batch sizes beyond 10 times (known as the 10X rule or Level 1 SUPAC limit) is important (especially for the products having high market volumes) to reduce the number of batches and improve the cost effectiveness. Hence, batch size of such products need to increase manufacturing scale as much as possible to reduce the number of batches as cost effective approach. This requires enhanced regulatory submissions, stability data, and validation to ensure product quality, safety, and efficacy remain unchanged. v. Improved flowability in Sterile gel formulation: Sterile gel formulation having criticality of flowability during travel through pipelines in plant scale manufacturing batches, as gel becomes solidify due to temperature drop during travel. Ophthalmic gel formulation faced technical challenges of flowability during traveling through pipelines from bulk manufacturing to filling line. vi. Ophthalmic suspension formulation: A sterile Otic suspension was developed using bead mill technology to achieve the desired particle size of around D(50): around 1 micron and D(90): around 3 micron. Critical parameter for Optimization is Particle size. vii. Rejuvenation of Brand: Febrex Plus Tablets (Enhanced Clinical Efficacy) Febrex Plus Tablets, an established commercial product, reformulated to achieve differentiation through an improved onset of action compared to competitor brands in the market. This objective was accomplished by incorporating specialized excipients and A N N U A L R E P O R T 2 0 2 5 - 2 0 2 6 88 optimizing their concentrations to enable rapid disintegration.

Page 90Open in PDF ↗

c0

The formulation was successfully converted into a fast-disintegrating tablet and evaluated clinically using scintigraphy studies in human subjects. The modified formulation demonstrated significantly faster disintegration and enhanced drug release, leading to a quicker onset of therapeutic action. Furthermore, clinical studies confirmed that the reformulated product is superior in terms of overall therapeutic efficacy compared to the existing formulation. This strategic rejuvenation strengthens the brand’s market positioning and enhances patient benefit. viii. Rebuilding of Brand: Cyclopam Tablets (Improved Disintegration Profile) Cyclopam Tablet was reformulated with the objective of achieving faster disintegration compared to competitor brands in the market. Suitable excipients were identified, and their concentrations were systematically optimized to enhance the disintegration performance. The product was redesigned as a fast-disintegrating tablet and evaluated through scintigraphy studies in human subjects. The results demonstrated improved disintegration and faster drug release characteristics. This enhancement is expected to provide a faster onset of action, thereby improving therapeutic effectiveness. The reformulated product supports brand rebuilding by strengthening its competitive advantage and improving patient outcomes. b. The benefits derived like product improvement, cost reduction, product development or import substitution; i. Simplification homogenization process in Oral suspension formulations: With use of advanced technology of IKA homogenizer followings technical changes performed: 1. Optimized screen size/type/sequence for effective homogenization purpose. 2. Reducer technology used at outlet of IKA homogenizer to restrict the flow of suspension through homogenizer, consequently, increase in residence time of suspension in homogenizer, leads to effective homogenization process. With implementation of above mentioned technical changes, the required particle size was achieved with minimum cycles of homogenization, leads to cost effective formulation. ii. Scalability beyond 10 X batch size helped in reducing significant testing costs: The scalability factor is applied for products Glimepiride Tablets & Allopurinol Tablets. Glimepiride Tablet, immediate release with low dose formulation are successfully scaled up from 30.00 L commercial batch size to 90.00 L batch size with utilization of scientific scale up tools. Report on Corporate Governance for the year ended March 31, 2026 INDOCO’S PHILOSOPHY ON CODE OF GOVERNANCE Indoco fully subscribes to the principles and spirit of Corporate Governance. The Company has adopted transparency, disclosure, accountability and ethics as its business practices. The management believes that these principles will enable it to achieve the long-term objectives and goals. As part of its Corporate Governance philosophy, Indoco focuses its energies in safeguarding the interests of its stakeholders by utilizing its resources for maximum benefits. The Company constantly reviews its Corporate Governance policy to not only comply with the business, legal and social framework in which it operates but also to implement the best international practices in that regard. This report is prepared in accordance with the provisions of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI Listing Regulations”) and the report contains the details of Corporate Governance systems and processes at Indoco Remedies Limited. There are no non-compliances of any requirements of Corporate Governance Report, as per sub-paras (2) to (10) of Schedule V Part C of the SEBI Listing Regulations. BOARD OF DIRECTORS Composition and Size: The Company’s policy is to have a proper blend of Executive and Non-Executive Directors to maintain independence of the Board and at the same time separate Board’s functions of governance from management. As at March 31, 2026 in compliance with Regulation 17 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, the Company’s Board of Directors headed by its Chairman - Mr. Suresh G Kare, comprises of seven Other Directors, out of which four Directors are Independent Non-Executive Directors. None of the Independent Directors of the Company serve as an Independent Director in more than seven listed companies. The Board confirms that the Independent Directors fulfil the conditions specified in the SEBI Listing Regulations and that they are Independent of the management. The day-to-day management of the Company is conducted by the Managing Director and Jt. Managing Director subject to the supervision, direction and control of the Board of Directors. The Directors are not related to each other in terms of the definition of “relative” under the Companies Act, 2013 (“Act”), except Ms. Aditi Panandikar, Managing Director who is the daughter of Mr. Suresh G 91 Kare, Chairman.

Transfer of unclaimed/unpaid amounts and shares to the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF): Pursuant to Sections 124 and 125 of the Act read with the Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority (Accounting, Audit, Transfer and Refund) Rules, 2016 (“IEPF Rules”), dividend, if not claimed for a period of seven years from the date of transfer to Unpaid Dividend Account of the Company, are liable to be transferred to IEPF. Further, all the shares in respect of which dividend has remained unclaimed for seven consecutive years or more from the date of transfer to unpaid dividend account shall also be transferred to IEPF Authority. The said requirement does not apply to shares in respect of which there is a specific order of Court, Tribunal or Statutory Authority, restraining any transfer of the shares. In the interest of the shareholders, the Company sends letters to the shareholders to claim their dividends in order to avoid transfer of dividends/shares to IEPF Authority. Notices in this regard are also published in the newspapers and the details of unclaimed dividends and shareholders whose shares are liable to be transferred to the IEPF Authority, are uploaded on the Company’s website at https://www.indoco.com/ inv-unpaid-dividend.asp and https://www.indoco.com/inv-IEPF.asp. In light of the aforesaid provisions, the Company has during the year, transferred to IEPF the unclaimed dividends, outstanding for seven years. Further, shares of the Company, in respect of which dividend has not been claimed for seven consecutive years or more from the date of transfer to unpaid dividend account, have also been transferred to the demat account of IEPF Authority. The details of unclaimed dividends and shares transferred to IEPF during Financial Year 2025-2026 are as follows: Financial Year | Amount of unclaimed dividend transferred (in `) | Number of Shares | Number of Shareholders 2017-2018 | 1,73,799 | 6,513 | 19 The Members who have a claim on above dividends and shares may claim the same from IEPF Authority by submitting an online application in web Form No. IEPF-5 available on the website www.iepf.gov.in and sending a physical copy of the same, duly signed to the Company, along with requisite documents enumerated in the web Form No. IEPF-5. No claims shall lie against the Company in respect of the dividend/shares so transferred. Governance, leadership and oversight 7. Statement by the director responsible for the business responsibility report, highlighting ESG-related challenges, targets and achievements (listed entity has flexibility regarding the placement of this disclosure) | Our world is undergoing a profound transformation. Climate challenges, tightening regulations, and shifting stakeholder expectations demand not just compliance, but conviction. At Indoco, we are meeting this moment by embedding sustainability into how we manufacture, how we govern, and how we grow. Growth, for us, must never come at the cost of our planet or our people. This has been a year of visible progress, and of honest reckoning. The most significant shift has been in our energy mix. Renewable sources now account for 43.5% of our total energy consumption, up from 23.9% in the previous year, driven by the introduction of briquettes as boiler fuel at selected sites and a decisive move away from carbon-intensive alternatives. This has translated directly into results: our Scope 1 emissions fell by 18.6%, and our combined Scope 1 and Scope 2 footprint declined by 8.8% even as production volumes rose. Water stewardship advanced on every front. Total water withdrawal reduced by 16.7%, from 4,07,900 to 3,39,737 kilolitres. The commissioning of a state-of-the-art Reverse Osmosis plant at our Patalganga site has materially expanded our wastewater treatment capacity, enabling the recycling of treated effluent and reducing our dependence on freshwater. Patalganga and our R&D Centre at Rabale now operate partial Zero Liquid Discharge systems. At another key facility, replacing water and steam ejectors with Dry Vacuum Pumps has delivered concurrent savings in electricity, water and emissions. Our digitalisation programme - TrackWise, SAP, DMS, LMS and digital signature solutions - has strengthened transparency and compliance while measurably reducing paper consumption across batch records and training documentation. We are also deploying intelligent platforms to monitor workforce safety and manage risk proactively. External validation followed. In March 2026, our Patalganga API manufacturing site was awarded a Bronze Medal in the EcoVadis Sustainability Rating, scoring 64 out of 100 and placing in the 67th percentile globally - an independent benchmark of our progress across environment, labour and human rights, ethics, and sustainable procurement. On our people, we recorded zero fatalities and zero high- consequence work-related injuries, alongside zero complaints relating to sexual harassment, child labour, forced labour, discrimination or wages. Provident Fund and Gratuity coverage stood at 100% for both employees and workers. I must equally be candid about where we have further to travel. Rising production volumes drove our absolute energy consumption up by 27.1% and our Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 20.2% - a reminder that efficiency gains alone will not decouple our growth from our footprint, and that the harder structural work 127

Page 129Open in PDF ↗

c0

lies ahead. Our sustainable sourcing framework is in its early stages: Our Supplier Code of Conduct now extends to our principal value chain partners, and building this into a structured programme of assessment and capability - building across the wider supplier base is work that lies before us. Our disclosures this year have not been externally assured. Each of these is a priority for the year ahead. To hold ourselves accountable, we have adopted the Indoco 2030 Strategic Targets, measured against a Financial Year 2025-2026 baseline: • Environmental Impact - reduce freshwater withdrawal by 3%; reduce energy consumption by 3%; reduce Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions by 3%. • Social & Human Capital - achieve zero workplace incidents and continuously improve safety performance; maintain zero human rights violations; maintain zero tolerance for child labour. • Corporate Governance - sustain zero incidents of data breaches, corruption and bribery. Detailed implementation plans and investment requirements for these targets are being finalised and will be reported from Financial Year 2026-2027. Sustainability at Indoco is not a parallel agenda. It is how we intend to remain a trusted manufacturer of medicines for the decades ahead. 8. 3. Describe the processes in place to safely reclaim your products for reusing, recycling and disposing at the end of life, for (a) Plastics (including packaging) (b) E-waste (c) Hazardous waste and (d) other waste. Plastics (including packaging): To promote reuse and minimize packaging waste, factory cartons are reused in the following manner: • Standard case lots of sales materials are dispatched to CFA locations using reusable factory cartons. • Loose cartons are retained and utilized during the repacking of sample consignments. • Central Warehouse (CWH) uses these loose cases for repacking sample materials and forwards them to CFAs for repacking of sales consignments to stockists. This reuse process helps in reducing shipper costs. We have established appropriate waste management systems across all our facilities. Our waste disposal processes adhere to local regulations and prioritize minimizing the amount of waste sent to landfills. Waste Type | Waste management procedure in place Plastic (including packaging) | Sent to authorized recyclers E-waste | Sold to authorized recyclers for safe disposal Hazardous Waste | Sent to authorized recyclers/Pre-processor for co-processing or to the TSDF (Treatment, Storage, and Disposal Facilities) site Other Waste | Sent to authorized recyclers Note: Indoco follows a structured process to minimize the risk of contamination to pharmaceutical products and to protect the environment. This process aligns with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), regulatory requirements, and Safety, Health, and Environmental (SHE) guidelines. i. Effluent Treatment • All Indoco manufacturing sites operate an Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) to treat effluents generated during manufacturing and testing. • Treated effluents are disposed of strictly in compliance with national and international environmental, health, and safety regulations. ii. Waste Collection and Storage • All waste is properly labeled and promptly destroyed to avoid cross-contamination. • Waste is not allowed to accumulate inside production areas. • Collected waste is placed in designated, suitable receptacles and transferred to external collection points. iii. Waste Disposal and Destruction • Pharmaceutical waste is destroyed under the supervision of a designated responsible person. • Critical waste, such as printed packaging material, is destroyed by tearing, shredding, or drilling. • At contract manufacturing sites, destruction is carried out in the presence of an Indoco representative. • Preferred destruction method is incineration, wherever applicable. • Deblistered strips and packaging materials are marked as scrap and destroyed by shredding. 133 • Laboratory waste is treated as per approved procedures before disposal.

Health and safety management system: a. Whether an occupational health and safety management system has been implemented by the entity? (Yes/ No). If yes, the coverage of such a system? Yes, the Company is committed to maintaining high standards of health, safety and well-being for all employees, contractors and stakeholders through a robust Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) Management System aligned with legal requirements and industry best practices. 137

A well-defined EHS Policy forms the foundation of this commitment and is communicated across the organization. A dedicated EHS Department, led by a qualified Safety person, ensures compliance and effective implementation of safety practices, supported by an EHS Committee that reviews performance and recommends improvements. Regular risk assessments are conducted to identify and mitigate workplace hazards and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) are established for all critical activities to ensure safe and consistent operations. A structured system for incident and near-miss reporting is in place, enabling root cause analysis and implementation of corrective actions. Employee health is supported through an on-site Occupational Health Centre, annual medical check-ups and pre-employment health assessments. Continuous training programs enhance employee awareness on safety practices, emergency response, and use of PPE, which is provided based on job requirements and strictly monitored. An Onsite Emergency Plan is implemented to address potential emergencies, supported by trained firefighting and first aid teams. Regular mock drills are conducted across all shifts to ensure preparedness and continual improvement. The coverage of the Company’s Occupational Health and Safety Management System is 100%. b. What are the processes used to identify work-related hazards and assess risks on a routine and non- routine basis by the entity? Indoco follows a proactive and systematic approach to identify, assess and control occupational health and safety risks, ensuring a safe working environment through continuous improvement. Health and safety is overseen by the Environmental, Health, Safety (EHS) team, which is responsible for developing and implementing policies, procedures and programs across all locations. Hazards are identified through regular workplace inspections by trained personnel, employee reporting mechanisms and analysis of past incidents and near misses. A well-defined Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) system is implemented to evaluate risks associated with products, activities and services, enabling structured risk prioritization and mitigation. Risk assessments are conducted for both routine and non-routine activities using likelihood and consequence evaluation, supported by a risk matrix. Both qualitative and quantitative methods are applied depending on the nature of the risks. In addition, specialized risk assessments such as HAZOP for Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient (API) processes, risk assessments for formulation units, and daily work permit system along with Job Safety Analysis (JSA) are carried out to ensure comprehensive hazard identification and control. All health and safety systems are subject to regular internal and external audits to ensure effectiveness and compliance. Supporting frameworks include a comprehensive Safety Manual, formal risk management policies and robust chemical safety protocols to ensure safe handling, storage and disposal in line with regulatory requirements. c. Whether you have processes for workers to report work-related hazards and to remove themselves from such risks. (Y/N) Yes, we provide mechanisms for employees and workers to report any work-related hazards or dangerous situations. Individuals can report near misses, injuries and incidents to their department heads. d. Do the employees/workers of the entity have access to non-occupational medical and healthcare services? (Yes/No) Yes, employees and workers of the Company have access to medical and healthcare services for non- occupational conditions. First aid kits are available in all departments to address minor injuries or ailments not related to work. Additionally, eligible employees and workers are covered under the Employees’ State Insurance Act, which provides support in cases of work-related injuries, illnesses, or maternity benefits.

Describe the processes for identifying key stakeholder groups of the entity. As a responsible Company, we are steadfast in our commitment to cultivating strong and meaningful relationships with stakeholders. PRINCIPLE 9 Businesses should engage with and provide value to their consumers in a responsible manner Essential Indicators 1. Describe the mechanisms in place to receive and respond to consumer complaints and feedback To Receive:  Mechanism for formulation sites - • Complaints can be communicated either orally or written form or through any other means of communication like electronically. • We have a dedicated email Id for each facility to receive consumer complaints. Once the complaints are received, the same are logged into the system. • Any additional information related to the complaint can be requested through a letter or an email.  Additionally for API sites, SOP No. SOP/PP/QA/051 is implemented for handling customer (Consumer) complaints: • The Marketing department forwards the complaint to the Plant QA team within 48 hours from the receipt of the complaint. The QA head then reviews the complaint and send an interim response to the complainant through the Marketing department. • Critical complaints are investigated within 15 working days, while non-critical ones are completed within 30 working days from the time the complaint is received. • Once the investigation is completed, feedback determining the satisfaction of the complainant is obtained. Management Discussion and Analysis Indian Pharmaceutical Industry The Indian pharmaceutical industry continued to consolidate its position as one of the fastest-growing and most strategically important sectors of the Indian economy during FY 2025–26. Supported by favourable demographics, rising healthcare expenditure, increasing prevalence of chronic diseases, robust policy support and a rapidly evolving innovation ecosystem, the industry demonstrated strong resilience despite persistent global macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties. Today, India is recognised as the Pharmacy of the World, supplying affordable and high-quality medicines to over 200 countries while maintaining its leadership in generic pharmaceuticals and vaccines. The country is the third-largest pharmaceutical producer globally by volume and among the top producers by value, accounting for nearly 20% of global generic medicine exports and supplying a significant share of the world’s vaccines and essential medicines. India’s globally competitive manufacturing base, large pool of scientific talent, strong regulatory capabilities and cost-efficient production ecosystem continue to strengthen its strategic importance within global healthcare supply chains. The Indian Pharmaceutical Market (IPM) maintained its growth trajectory during FY2025-26, expanding to `2.57 lakh crore from `2.33 lakh crore in FY2024-25 (IQVIA DATA), registering a healthy 9.9% YOY growth while delivering a four-year CAGR of approximately 8.4%. The industry continues to outperform several other manufacturing sectors, supported by structural rather than cyclical growth drivers. Unlike previous growth cycles that were largely volume-driven, the pharmaceutical industry is increasingly witnessing a transition towards value-led expansion. Demand is progressively shifting from acute therapies towards chronic disease management, speciality pharmaceuticals, biologics, biosimilars and complex formulations. Simultaneously, increasing healthcare awareness, wider health insurance coverage, digital healthcare adoption and greater accessibility to quality healthcare across Tier II and Tier III cities are expanding the addressable market. The industry is also experiencing a structural transformation driven by technology. artificial intelligence, machine learning, advanced analytics and automation are increasingly being integrated across the pharmaceutical value chain-from drug discovery and clinical trial optimisation to manufacturing, quality assurance, and pharmacovigilance and supply chain management. These technological advancements are expected to significantly improve productivity, reduce development timelines and enhance operational efficiencies over the coming years. India’s emergence as a preferred alternative manufacturing destination under the global China Plus One sourcing strategy continues to strengthen its position within international pharmaceutical supply chains. Global pharmaceutical companies are increasingly diversifying sourcing and manufacturing operations, creating significant opportunities for Indian manufacturers across Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs), complex formulations, biologics and Contract Development and Manufacturing Organisation (CDMO) services Industry Highlights The Indian pharmaceutical market recorded broad-based growth across most major therapy segments during MAT March 2026, reflecting both improving healthcare access and changing disease patterns. Government Initiatives The Government of India continues to strengthen the pharmaceutical ecosystem through targeted policy initiatives focused on manufacturing competitiveness, healthcare accessibility and innovation. 153

Page 155Open in PDF ↗

c0

Major initiatives include: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme encouraging domestic manufacturing of high-value • pharmaceutical products and advanced drug formulations. PLI Scheme for Bulk Drugs and establishment of Bulk Drug Parks, aimed at reducing import • dependence for critical APIs and strengthening supply chain resilience. Medical Device Parks Scheme, promoting domestic manufacturing and reducing import dependency • for medical technologies. Ayushman Bharat, the world’s largest publicly funded health assurance programme, significantly • improving healthcare accessibility. Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP), expanding access to affordable quality • generic medicines across the country. Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, enabling integrated digital health records and technology-enabled • healthcare delivery. • Continued focus on strengthening domestic R&D capabilities, biotechnology innovation, vaccine research and pharmaceutical infrastructure. These initiatives are expected to significantly improve India’s global competitiveness while encouraging innovation, self-reliance and long-term investment. Strengths Global Manufacturing Dominance: India is the largest provider of generic drugs globally and supplies over 60% of the world’s vaccine demand. Massive Cost Advantage: Production costs in India remain 33–40% lower than in Western nations, supported by highly efficient process chemistry and a vast pool of skilled, English-speaking scientists. Highest Number of USFDA Plants: Outside the United States, India hosts the largest number of USFDA- compliant manufacturing facilities, ensuring structural readiness for heavily regulated export markets. Weakness Heavy Raw Material Dependence: Despite domestic efforts, Indian drugmakers still rely on China for nearly 60–70% of their Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) and Key Starting Materials (KSMs), leaving the supply chain vulnerable to external shocks. Low Innovation Capital: Indian firms historically spend about 7–8% of their revenues on R&D, compared to the 15–25% standard for global blockbuster drug innovators. The market remains deeply rooted in process innovation rather than novel molecule discovery. Fragmented Domestic Market: The domestic space is intensely fragmented with thousands of small to medium enterprises. This fragmentation triggers severe price competition, lowering profit margins in the value tier Opportunities The Biosimilars & Biologics Wave: Biologics are growing at a rapid CAGR of nearly 16%. With massive global patent expires on major biologics hitting over the next few years, Indian biopharma companies A N N U A L R E P O R T 2 0 2 5 - 2 0 2 6 154 have a massive window to capture the complex biosimilar space.

Government Policy Tailwinds: Schemes like the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) for Bulk Drugs and the newly launched Biopharma SHAKTI initiative ($1.2 billion outlay) are aggressively funding R&D, clinical infrastructure, and API self-reliance. Expanding Healthcare Access: Driven by rising disposable incomes and schemes like Ayushman Bharat, local health insurance coverage has climbed past 40% in both rural and urban areas. This has unlocked massive structural domestic demand for primary and chronic care therapies. Threats Stringent Price Controls: The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) closely regulates essential medicine prices in India. Expanding price control caps directly impact profit margins on domestic product portfolios. Tightening Global Quality Standards: Overseas regulatory bodies (like the USFDA and EDQM) are continuously raising compliance bars. Recent structural upgrades in India like the mandatory implementation of the revised Schedule M guidelines aim to fix this, but compliance costs can strain smaller players. Geo-Political and Trade Vulnerabilities: Trade disputes, fluctuating freight dynamics, and rising protectionist policies in Western economies present persistent risks to India’s $30+ billion export engine. a) Internal control system and their adequacy: The Company has an Internal Control System, commensurate with the size of its operations. Indoco SPADE The Indoco SPADE division recorded 6.1% growth and attained a 3.9% market share, while gaining the 12th position in the covered market. The division generated 2.72 crore prescriptions, adding 10.9 lakh incremental prescriptions through a network of over 67,000 prescribers, reflecting sustained brand equity and expanding market penetration. Innovation remained a key growth driver during the year. New Febrex Plus, launched with proprietary Velosorb technology, strengthened the division’s leadership in the cough and cold segment. Supported by positive clinical evidence from the FAST study, the brand delivered 1.12 crore prescriptions and continued to gain traction across key geographies. The division’s growth was further supported by strong performances from strategic brands, including CLATM, FEDRIS, DROPIZIN and VOPANZA, while new product launches contributed 13% of the total sales, significantly ahead of industry benchmarks and reinforcing the effectiveness of the Division’s innovation-led portfolio strategy. Notably, CLATM improved its market ranking from 12 to 6, delivering strong value growth, while VOPANZA 20 continued to strengthen its position in the rapidly expanding Vonoprazan market. FEDRIS emerged as one of the successful recent launches, reflecting robust physician acceptance and market penetration. Supported by resilient core brands, successful new launches and an innovation-led growth strategy, the Indoco SPADE division is building a scalable platform for long-term value creation. Continued investments in portfolio expansion and market penetration are expected to drive sustainable growth in the years ahead. AnaCipher (CRO) AnaCipher’s state-of-the-art infrastructure, spanning 40,000 sq ft, has undergone successful inspections and approvals from several global regulatory agencies, multiple times. These include: USFDA, UKMHRA, WHO, EMA (Netherlands, France, Denmark & Finland), MoH-Oman & CDSCO (India) Additionally, AnaCipher has achieved product-specific approvals from regulatory bodies in Algeria, Australia (TGA), Belarus, Canada (TPD), China (NPRA), Costa Rica, Indonesia, Lebanon, Libya, Malaysia (NPRA), South Africa, Taiwan, and Ukraine. AnaCipher’s dedicated Pharmacovigilance unit provides end‑to‑end drug safety services across the product lifecycle, from clinical development through post‑marketing. The CRO’s validated PV database (21 CFR Part 11 and GAMP compliant) currently supports safety monitoring for around 1,000 products across highly regulated and emerging global markets, covering activities such as ICSR case processing, aggregate safety reporting, signal and risk management, and QPPV/MAH support. AnaCipher has undergone multiple successful inspections by leading global regulatory agencies— such as the USFDA, UK MHRA, WHO, EMA member states, GCC and CDSCO, among others—and, in total, the facility has now cleared more than seventeen inspections and audits from international regulatory bodies and accreditation agencies in last seven years, including NABL for its clinical laboratory. AnaCipher has also successfully completed an inspection by ANVIS, Brazil’s national health surveillance agency, and formal approval is expected shortly, further strengthening its global regulatory credentials. On the clinical side, the facility is organised into four independent Clinical Pharmacology units with capacities of 20, 30, 48 and 48 beds, a total of 146 beds, respectively, enabling it to run multiple projects in parallel and collectively handle around 10 studies per month under GCP‑compliant conditions with a volunteer pool of over 26,000 participants, including more than 1,000 females. AnaCipher conducts studies under biometric cross‑participation controls, 24/7 supervision by qualified physicians and with seamless access to tertiary hospital care whenever required. Bioanalytical operations are supported by a portfolio of over 250 validated methods, reflecting a robust and highly experienced team capable of handling a wide range of small‑molecule and complex assays. The centre operates on 21 CFR Part 11‑compliant platforms with GAMP‑based computer system validation, a three‑tier data‑backup framework and continuous temperature monitoring across critical areas, and has recently completed an ANVISA (Brazil) inspection, with formal approval expected shortly Indoco Analytical Solutions (IAS), Rabale Operating from Indoco’s R&D Centre at Rabale, this premier, Indian FDA and USFDA-approved public testing laboratory continues to advance its state-of-the-art testing capabilities. Demonstrating its exceptional regulatory compliance status, IAS successfully cleared 32 customer audits and one state FDA audit over the past year. Backed by this robust operational excellence, the facility has significantly expanded its analytical spectrum to address critical, emerging global regulatory shifts. The laboratory remains at the forefront of complex impurity profiling, having successfully completed more than 50 Nitrosamine and Nitrosamine Drug Substance Related Impurity (NDSRI) projects for its global clientele last year. In a rapid response to recent regulatory mandates for liquid oral finished dosage forms (FDFs), IAS deployed high-sensitivity testing frameworks for the immediate screening and quantification of Ethylene Glycol (EG) and Diethylene Glycol (DEG). Additionally, the facility has strengthened its compendial compliance suite by establishing specialized capabilities for the critical analysis of Talc to detect asbestos content, strictly adhering to updated pharmacopeial requirements. The laboratory has also augmented its core pharmaceutical testing services by integrating expert physicochemical characterization, offering precise determinations of partition coefficient (log P) and dissociation constant (pKa). These newly integrated milestones complement the laboratory’s established technical offerings. IAS remains a key partner for complex Genotoxic and Azido impurity screening, including specialized NAP testing for APIs lacking commercial reference standards-alongside in silico toxicity predictions. The division continues to deliver comprehensive elemental impurity assessments under ICH Q3D, unknown impurity isolation, thermal analysis, and solid-state crystallographic polymorphism studies for patent evaluations. Furthermore, IAS drives generic development pipelines through robust de- formulation studies of RLDs and extractable and leachable (E&L) evaluations for complex drug-device combinations. Indoco Analytical Solutions (Stability Testing Centre), Chatrapati Sambhaji Nagar Indoco Analytical Solutions, located at MIDC, Waluj, Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar (Aurangabad), is a strategic centre of excellence that provides centralised stability testing support for drug substances and drug products manufactured across all production facilities of Indoco. Spread across a plot area of 8,100 sq. m. with a built-up area of 3,420 sq. m., the facility contains state-of-the-art analytical and microbiology laboratories, along with nine stability chambers. The stability chambers have a combined operational capacity of about 22 lakh litres, complemented by a backup capacity of 3.64 lakh litres, ensuring business continuity and uninterrupted stability study operations. Designed to meet global regulatory expectations, IAS operates under controlled HVAC systems that maintain consistent environmental conditions, thereby ensuring the integrity, reliability, and accuracy of analytical and microbiological testing. The facility is supported by a robust Quality Management System, developed and maintained in compliance with GLP, reinforcing operational excellence, data integrity, and regulatory compliance.

Independent Auditors’ Report to the Members of Indoco Remedies Limited Report on the Audit of the Standalone Financial Statements Opinion We have audited the accompanying standalone financial statements of INDOCO REMEDIES LIMITED (the “Company”), which comprise the Balance Sheet as at March 31, 2026, the Statement of Profit and Loss (including Other Comprehensive Income), the Statement of Changes in Equity and the Statement of Cash Flows for the year ended on that date and notes to the financial statements (including summary of material accounting policies and other explanatory information (hereinafter referred to as the “standalone financial statements”). In our opinion and to the best of our information and according to the explanations given to us, the aforesaid standalone financial statements give the information required by the Companies Act, 2013 (the “Act”) in the manner so required and give a true and fair view in conformity with the Indian Accounting Standards prescribed under section 133 of the Act read with the Companies (Indian Accounting Standards) Rules, 2015, as amended, (“Ind AS”) and other accounting principles generally accepted in India, of the state of affairs of the Company as at March 31, 2026 and its Loss, total comprehensive income, changes in equity and its cash flows for the year ended on that date. Basis for Opinion We conducted our audit of the standalone financial statements in accordance with the Standards on Auditing (“SA”s) specified under section 143(10) of the Act. Our responsibilities under those Standards are further described in the Auditor’s Responsibilities for the Audit of the standalone financial statements section of our report. We are independent of the Company in accordance with the Code of Ethics issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (“ICAI”) together with the ethical requirements that are relevant to our audit of the standalone financial statements under the provisions of the Act and the Rules made thereunder, and we have fulfilled our other ethical responsibilities in accordance with these requirements and the ICAI’s Code of Ethics. We believe that the audit evidence obtained by us is sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for our audit opinion on the standalone financial statements. Sr. No. | Key Audit Matters | Auditor’s Response 1 | Provisions for Sales Returns The Company provides for sales returns on an estimated basis as a percentage of sales. Such an estimate is arrived at on the basis of average of actual sales return over the last 3 financial years. Such estimation is based on management’s best judgement of the probability of sales returns. Provision for sales returns amounted to ` 2,444.82 lakhs as on March 31, 2026 ` 2,262.28 lakhs as on March 31, 2025. Refer note no. 29: current provisions to the standalone financial statements. | Principal Audit Procedures Performed We have carried out the validation of the information provided by the management by performing the following procedures: a) Validating the process consistently implemented by the management in arriving at the estimates. b) Correlating the amounts of actual sales returns with the provisions made. c) Evaluated management assessment for change in estimates for provision for sales return during this year. d) Getting representations from the management wherever necessary. 2 | Intangible Assets Under Development The Company undertakes several projects for new product development. Once the development is complete as per management assessment, such items are reclassified as Intangible Assets in the books of accounts. The management makes an assessment as to whether all such projects are capable of being completed and capable of getting the requisite regulatory approvals. On the basis of such assessment, the costs incurred on such projects till the time development is complete as per management assessment, are reflected in the financial statements as “Intangible assets under development”. The quantum of Intangible Assets Under Development as on March 31,2026 was ` 6,172.25 lakhs (` 4,441.79 lakhs as on March 31, 2025). Information Other than the Standalone Financial Statements and Auditor’s Report Thereon The Company’s Board of Directors is responsible for the other information. The other information comprises the information included in the Management Discussion and Analysis, Board’s Report including Annexures to Board’s Report, Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report, Corporate Governance and Shareholder’s Information, but does not include the standalone financial statements and our auditor’s report thereon. Our opinion on the standalone financial statements does not cover the other information and we do not express any form of assurance conclusion thereon. In connection with our audit of the standalone financial statements, our responsibility is to read the other information and, in doing so, consider whether the other information is materially inconsistent with the standalone financial statements or our knowledge obtained during the course of our audit or otherwise appears to be materially misstated. If, based on the work we have performed, we conclude that there is a material misstatement of this other information, we are required to report that fact. We have nothing to report in this regard. Responsibilities of the Management and those charged with governance for the Standalone Financial Statements The Company’s Board of Directors is responsible for the matters stated in section 134(5) of the Act with respect to the preparation of these standalone financial statements that give a true and fair view of the financial position, financial performance, including other comprehensive income, changes in equity and cash flows of the Company in accordance with the Ind AS and other accounting principles generally accepted in India. This responsibility also includes maintenance of adequate accounting records in accordance with the provisions of the Act for safeguarding the assets of the Company and for preventing and detecting frauds and other irregularities; selection and application of appropriate accounting policies; making judgments and estimates that are reasonable and prudent; and design, implementation and maintenance of adequate internal financial controls, that were operating effectively for ensuring the accuracy and completeness of the accounting records, relevant to the preparation and presentation of the standalone financial statements that give a true and fair view and are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error. In preparing the standalone financial statements, management is responsible for assessing the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern, disclosing, as applicable, matters related to going concern and using the going concern basis of accounting unless management either intends to liquidate the Company or to cease operations, or has no realistic alternative but to do so. The Board of Directors is also responsible for overseeing the Company’s financial reporting process. Auditors’ Responsibilities for the Audit of the Standalone Financial Statements Our objectives are to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the standalone financial statements as a whole are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error, and to issue an auditor’s report that includes our opinion. Reasonable assurance is a high level of assurance, but is not a guarantee that an audit conducted in accordance with SAs will always detect a material misstatement when it exists. Misstatements can arise from fraud or error and are considered material if, individually or in the aggregate, they could reasonably be expected to influence the economic decisions of users taken on the basis of these A N N U A L R E P O R T 2 0 2 5 - 2 0 2 6 174 standalone financial statements.
